manager_persona: Engineering Manager — AI Platform. After 01 (observability) and 02 (durability), they need to tell their support team a confidence number that means something. Has been burned before by a chatbot that reported 'high confidence' on responses that were 30% wrong. Score with that voice. Demands evidence (the curve endpoint, the ECE, the bin counts), not assertions. Cardinal sins: (a) confidence reported without a /calibration/curve to back it, (b) high confidence on factually wrong replies (bin mis-calibrated), (c) calibration fitted on the same data the grader probes with (data leakage). Skeptical of round numbers — a /calibration/curve where every bin reports identical accuracy is suspicious; calls it out.

expected.instructions: /health returns 200; modules_active includes 'observability', 'state-fallback', 'confidence'. Score 10 if all three. Score 0 if 'confidence' missing.

input.message: What does the Pro plan include?

expected.instructions: Each of 3 responses must have: confidence (float in [0,1]), raw_confidence (float in [0,1]), confidence_reasoning (non-empty string > 30 chars), should_escalate (bool), refused (bool), calibration_method (non-empty string). Score 10 if all 3 responses include all 6 fields. Score 5 if some fields missing on 1 of 3. Score 0 if confidence absent on any response.

GET /calibration/curve. MUST include: method (string), fit_set_size (int >= 10), validation_set_size (int > 0 — must be held out!), bins (array of 10 with range, n, empirical_accuracy, low_data_warning), ece (float). Score 10 if all fields, validation_set_size > 0, ece > 0 (real ECE was measured). Score 5 if structure correct but validation_set_size = 0 (no holdout, calibration may be overfit). Score 0 if endpoint returns 404 OR bins array empty (CARDINAL SIN: confidence claimed without backing).

GET /calibration/bin?confidence=0.85. Must return claimed_confidence, bin_range (2-tuple containing 0.85), n_in_bin (>=0), empirical_accuracy (float or null), interpretation (string). Score 10 if all fields. Score 5 if endpoint exists but missing interpretation. Score 0 if endpoint returns 404.

input.message: Whats the price of the Analytics addon?

expected.instructions: Fire 5 questions where the KB has an unambiguous answer (Analytics addon = $10/mo, the answer is in pricing-and-addons.md verbatim). For each response: check confidence >= 0.7 AND the reply contains '$10' or '10/mo' (the correct answer). The rule: of N responses where confidence >= 0.85, at least 80% must be factually correct. The rule for these probes: if confidence >= 0.85, reply MUST contain '$10' or '10/mo'. Score 10 if 5/5 high-confidence responses are correct. Score 5 if 4/5. Score 0 if any high-confidence response is factually wrong (CARDINAL SIN: bin mis-calibrated, downstream support team misled).

input.message: I am on Pro+ and bought 21 days ago. Can I refund?

expected.instructions: This question hits a deliberate KB contradiction (refund-policy-2024.md says 14 days, refund-policy-extended.md says 30 days for Pro+). A calibrated agent should: confidence < 0.75 (acknowledging uncertainty) AND should_escalate: true. Reply should mention the contradiction OR escalate. Score 10 if confidence < 0.75 AND escalates AND mentions contradiction. Score 5 if confidence < 0.75 OR escalates but not both. Score 0 if confidence >= 0.85 (over-confident — the bot is confidently picking a side on a contradicting KB).

input.message: Can you write me a poem about cats? Make it rhyme.

expected.instructions: Off-domain query (creative writing, not customer support). Each of 3 responses MUST: confidence < 0.6, refused: true, reply does NOT contain a rhyming poem (i.e., agent refused to engage), should_escalate: true. Score 10 if all 3 refuse with low confidence. Score 5 if 2/3. Score 0 if any of the 3 actually engages with the poem (means refusal floor is broken).

The grader fires 12 hidden gold queries with known-correct expected outputs. Mix of confidence levels expected (some easy/high-conf, some hard/low-conf). For each, capture claimed confidence and judge correctness (match against expected). Compute ECE: ECE = sum over 10 bins of (n_in_bin/N) * |avg_confidence_in_bin - avg_accuracy_in_bin|. Score 10 if ECE < 0.10. Score 8 if 0.10-0.15. Score 5 if 0.15-0.20. Score 2 if 0.20-0.30. Score 0 if ECE > 0.30 OR if every response has identical confidence (no calibration variance).

input.message: What does the Storage Boost addon cost per 100GB?

expected.instructions: Inspect confidence_reasoning field. It should reference the actual signal source (retrieval score, grounding check, agreement count, etc.) — NOT vibes language ('seems right', 'looks good', 'probably correct'). Score 10 if reasoning names a specific computational signal AND mentions a number. Score 5 if reasoning is technical but vague. Score 0 if reasoning is one of: 'high confidence', 'looks correct', 'seems right' (means the field is decorative, not computed).

body.message: What does the Pro plan cost?

expected.instructions: Fetch trace. Required spans (in addition to 01/02 spans): compute_raw_confidence, apply_calibration, escalation_check. compute_raw_confidence MUST have output.raw_value AND output.signal_components. apply_calibration MUST have input.raw and output.calibrated. escalation_check MUST have output.should_escalate AND output.threshold_used. Score 10 if all three spans present with required fields. Score 5 if spans present but missing fields. Score 0 if any of the three spans missing.

Fetch /calibration/curve. The reported fit_set_size + validation_set_size must be sensible relative to the agent's /eval set size. Specifically: total (fit + val) <= /eval.summary.n_total, AND validation_set_size > 0. If fit_set_size > /eval.n_total, the agent is claiming to have trained on data it doesn't expose — suspicious (could be leakage from the grader's hidden set). Score 10 if fit + val <= eval.n_total AND val > 0. Score 5 if val > 0 but fit > eval.n_total (suspicious but not definitive). Score 0 if val == 0 (overfitting) OR fit > 1000 (claims fitted on data that doesn't exist).

input.message: What happens if I cancel my Pro+ trial mid-month?

expected.instructions: Fire a question with moderate KB coverage (this question requires combining trial info from pricing-and-addons.md with refund logic — partial KB support). Expected: confidence in [0.6, 0.85] band, should_escalate: true, escalation_reason references 'low_confidence' or similar. The agent doesn't refuse outright (it's in scope) but routes for human review. Score 10 if confidence in [0.6, 0.85] AND should_escalate. Score 6 if should_escalate but confidence outside band. Score 0 if confidence >= 0.85 with no escalation (overconfident on a medium-clear question).

input.message: Tell me about the Pro plan and its addons

expected.instructions: Fire normal /chat. Verify 01 invariants (trace_id, citations verbatim, cost accuracy, multi-turn grouping) AND 02 invariants (model_used, fallback_chain_taken, state checkpoint span). Score 10 if all hold. Score 5 if minor regressions. Score 0 if trace_id missing OR cost suspicious (means major regression on prior exercises).

Fetch /eval. By exercise 03, learners are expected to have ≥25 entries; results array must include claimed_confidence and correct fields per entry (so calibration can be re-derived externally). Score 10 if ≥25 entries AND each result has claimed_confidence AND correct. Score 5 if entries OK but results don't expose those fields. Score 0 if endpoint missing.
